notes: §1985:VIII.4.2.4 GR2 puts a relative file in the non-sequential category: CLOSE is A (implementor closing operations, labels by the implementor's convention) and CLOSE WITH LOCK is A,B, "The file is locked and cannot be opened again during this execution of this run unit" (a later OPEN is status 38, §1985:VIII.1.3.4). SequentialIoBinder#BindClose refuses REEL/UNIT/NO REWIND on a non-sequential file (COBOL1693; the 1985 relative format has only WITH LOCK); FileRegistry#CloseByFormat executes the non-unit cell (close file, 42 when not open), FileRegistry#CloseWithLock locks only after a successful close, and FileRegistry#SharedOpenAttempt answers 38 for a locked name until the run unit's Reset. Probes at 85: random and dynamic access, LABEL RECORDS STANDARD and OMITTED; CLOSE and CLOSE WITH LOCK of an unopened file -> 42 and the file then opens 00; after WITH LOCK, OPEN INPUT, I-O and OUTPUT each -> 38 with USE run; CLOSE of the locked file -> 42; the lock survives CANCEL and re-CALL of the locking subprogram (38) and does not reach a same-named file of another program (00); CLOSE REEL, UNIT FOR REMOVAL, NO REWIND refused, bare CLOSE refused. The witness writes, reads, closes, closes WITH LOCK and gets 38 in the USE procedure. || REFUTED: DIVERGES (wrong-answer): CLOSE WITH LOCK must lock the physical file for the rest of the run unit; an OPEN of that physical file through any other file-name or file connector (same or another program) must be unsuccessful with I-O status 38. Repro refute-rd-05/c3b.cob: expected 'Y OPEN SAME PHYSICAL 38' and 'N OPEN SAME PHYSICAL 38'; observed 00 and a successful READ. The same sentence is in the sequential and indexed CLOSE rules (1985 transcription lines 16459 and 19068) and the report-file CLOSE (24235): sibling sweep. kb/Work PB5210 holds the defect (code read: coderead-85/out-read4/rd-05.json, refuter coderead-85/out-read4/rd-05-refute.json).
